chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:

Indeed, when news of the death of Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon him, and Zayd ibn Ḥārithah came to the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, whenever he entered his house, his weeping for them would greatly increase, and he would say, ‘They used to speak with me and keep me company, and now they have both gone together.’

key_terms.بُكَاؤُهُ: his weeping; the Prophet’s intense expression of grief
key_terms.فَذَهَبَا: so they both went; meaning they passed away
key_terms.وَفَاةُ: death; the passing away of a person
key_terms.يُؤَانِسَانِي: they used to bring me comfort and companionship
key_terms.يُحَدِّثَانِي: they used to speak with me; converse with me

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم grieve for Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib and Zayd ibn Ḥārithah?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the deep grief of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم upon the deaths of Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام and Zayd ibn Ḥārithah. It highlights his human sorrow, loyalty, and affection for those who were close companions and sources of comfort to him.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.527 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"When The Prophet (sw) received news of the deaths of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (as) and Zayd ibn Harithah, he would weep intensely when he entered his house and would say,
'They used to converse with me and bring me comfort, and now they are both gone.'"
